info.title: Fleetwire API
info.description:
# Fleetwire API

Read your fleet's listings, availability and bookings, and block dates or change booking status from your own systems.

## Authentication

Create a token in the dashboard under **Settings → Security → API Tokens**: https://app.fleetwire.io/settings/security/api-tokens

Send it as a bearer token on every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN
Accept: application/json
```

A token acts as the user who created it, scoped to that user's company. Treat it like a password: keep it server-side, never put it in browser or mobile code, and delete it from the dashboard if it leaks.

## Token scopes

When you create a token you choose its access:

| Access | Scopes | Can |
|---|---|---|
| Full access | `*` | Everything the user can do. Use this for Zapier. |
| Read only | `read` | Every `GET` endpoint |
| Custom | `read` plus any of the below | Read, plus the writes you pick |

Write scopes:

- `bookings:write` — booking status, blocked dates, notes, payment requests
- `customers:write` — create and update customers
- `webhooks:write` — create, change and delete webhook endpoints
- `pricing:write` — set and clear per-day listing prices

A request outside the token's scopes gets `403` with the missing scope in `message`. Scopes narrow a token; they never grant more than the user who created it has.

## Plan requirement

Reading works on every paid plan and during a free trial: any `GET`, with a token that has `read`.

Changing data (any request that needs a write scope such as `bookings:write`) needs the **Premium** plan.

Both cases are refused with `402 Payment Required`. Without an active subscription:

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "No subscription", "errors": ["You do not have an active subscription"] }
```

A write request on a plan below Premium:

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Your subscription does not support this feature.", "errors": ["Your subscription does not support this feature."] }
```

## Base URL

`https://api.fleetwire.io/api/v2`

## Rate limits

200 requests per minute per token. Over the limit you receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 401 | Missing or invalid token |
| 402 | No active subscription, or a write request on a plan below Premium |
| 403 | The token's user lacks permission for this action |
| 404 | Record not found, or it belongs to another company |
| 422 | Validation failed — see `errors` for the field messages |
| 429 | Rate limited |

Validation errors look like:

```json
{ "message": "The trip end field is required.", "errors": { "trip_end": ["The trip end field is required."] } }
```

## Dates and times

`trip_start` / `trip_end` are local wall-clock times (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) in the listing's timezone, returned alongside as `timezone`. `created_at` / `updated_at` are UTC ISO 8601. Money values are in **cents**.

## Webhooks

Rather than polling, register an endpoint (see the **Webhooks** folder) and Fleetwire POSTs a JSON body to it when something happens. Events:

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `reservation.created` | A booking is made, or a request is approved |
| `reservation.requested` | A booking request needs your approval |
| `reservation.canceled` | A booking is canceled |
| `booking.updated` | Dates, vehicle, customer or total change. `changed` lists the fields. |
| `booking.status_changed` | Any status change. Includes `previous_status`. |
| `trip.started` | A booking is marked started |
| `trip.ended` | A started trip is returned or completed |
| `payment.processed` | A payment succeeds |
| `payment.failed` | A charge is declined |
| `payment.refunded` | A payment is refunded |
| `customer.created` | A customer is added |
| `customer.updated` | A customer's name, email, phone, birth date or address changes. `changed` lists the fields. |

Booking events deliver the booking's `b_id`, `l_id`, `r_id`, `status`, `source`, `days`, `total` (cents), `trip_start`, `trip_end`, `timezone` and `listing_name`. Fetch anything else with `GET /bookings?b_id=…`.

**Headers on every delivery**

- `fleetwire-event` — the event name
- `fleetwire-event-id` — unique per event and the same on every retry; use it to ignore duplicates
- `fleetwire-occurred-at` — ISO 8601
- `fleetwire-delivery-attempt` — 1 to 5
- `fleetwire-signature` — `t=<unix time>,v1=<hex HMAC>`

**Verifying the signature.** Compute HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw request body>` with the endpoint's signing secret (`whsec_…`, returned once when you create the endpoint) and compare it with `v1` using a constant-time comparison. Reject deliveries whose `t` is more than 5 minutes old.

```js
const [t, v1] = header.split(',').map((part) => part.split('=')[1]);
const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex');
const valid = crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(v1));
```

**Retries.** Answer with any `2xx` within 30 seconds. A `5xx`, `408`, `425`, `429` or a timeout is retried up to 5 attempts over about 20 minutes (a numeric `Retry-After` is honoured). Other `4xx` responses are not retried. Every attempt appears in `GET /webhooks/:id/deliveries`.

## Zapier

Prefer no-code? The Fleetwire Zapier app covers new bookings, new customers, trip reminders and more without writing code.


## Partner API

For toll, violation and fee services working with many Fleetwire hosts. Partner endpoints live under `/partners/v1` and take a partner key (`fwp_…`), not a host API token. Fleetwire issues partner keys; email hi@fleetwire.io. Sandbox: `https://staging.fleetwire.io/api/partners/v1`.

One API for every toll, violation and fee service that bills rental companies' renters through Fleetwire.

Each partner gets one key and can work with every Fleetwire rental company that turned the partner on
(in Fleetwire: **Connections → Toll and violation partners**). Rental companies don't create tokens or paste keys.

**Fleetwire bills the renter.** A charge you send is added to the rental's order and invoiced to the renter
by the rental company's own rules. You don't charge renters directly, and you never see renter names or
contact details.

### Flow
1. A rental company turns your integration on.
2. `GET /companies` lists the companies that have you on.
3. `GET /companies/{company_id}/vehicles` gives the plates to watch.
4. `GET /companies/{company_id}/rentals` (optional) says which rental had a plate at a moment.
5. `POST /companies/{company_id}/charges` sends a toll, violation or fee, with its receipt.
6. `PATCH /companies/{company_id}/charges/{external_id}` changes it later.

### Toll plans
Each rental has a `toll_plan` that says how the renter pays for tolls. Check it before you send a toll:
- `unlimited`: the renter prepaid unlimited tolls. Don't add individual tolls to the rental.
- `activation_plus_toll`: an activation fee, then each actual toll. Send each toll.
- `pay_per_use`: each toll plus the rental company's per-toll fee. Send each toll, with your fee in `provider_fee_cents` if you charge one.
- `null`: the rental company hasn't set a plan. Hold the toll for review. Don't guess.

The rental company sets a default and can change it on any rental. Treat a value you don't recognize like `null`.

### Conventions
- **Money:** whole cents as integers, USD unless `currency` says otherwise. `$2.50` is `250`.
- **Times:** ISO 8601 with a UTC offset or `Z`.
- **Plates:** send them as printed. We compare case-insensitively, ignoring spaces and dashes.
- **Idempotency:** charges are keyed on your `external_id`, so sending the same charge twice is safe.
- **Rate limit:** 600 requests per minute per key. Over the limit you get `429` with `Retry-After`.
- **Turned off:** when a company turns you off, every endpoint for it answers `404 company_not_connected`
  at once. Stop sending for that company. Charges you already sent stay on their rentals.

### Planned
Webhooks from Fleetwire (`company.activated`, `company.deactivated`, `vehicle.added`, `vehicle.removed`,
`vehicle.plate_changed`, `rental.ended`). Until then, poll `GET /companies` and `GET /vehicles` (daily is plenty).

put.description:
**Scope:** `pricing:write`

Sets the nightly price for specific dates — for dynamic pricing tools. Up to 400 dates per call; a date sent again replaces its price.

- `prices` (array, required) — `[{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "price_in_cents": 14900}]`. Dates from yesterday on; prices are whole cents.

`applies_at_checkout` is `false` when the listing isn't priced by the day (fixed, free, tiered or hourly pricing) — the prices are saved but checkout won't use them until it is. Read prices back with `GET /listings/:l_id/daily-pricing`.

date.description: `Y-m-d`, from yesterday on. Each date once.

delete.description:
**Scope:** `pricing:write`

Returns the given dates to the listing's default price.

- `dates` (array, required) — `["YYYY-MM-DD", …]`, up to 400

post.description:
**Scope:** `bookings:write`

Blocks a listing for a time range — maintenance, shop time, a booking taken elsewhere.

**Body**

- `trip_start` (string, required) — local start time
- `trip_end` (string, required) — local end time, on or after `trip_start`
- `source` (object, required) — where to apply the block. `direct: true` blocks it in Fleetwire; `turo` / `getaround` / `outdoorsy: true` also push the block to that connected marketplace listing. Unknown keys are rejected.
- `notes` (string, optional, max 255)

The response reports, per channel, whether the block was attempted and succeeded.

trip_end.description: End of the block, on or after `trip_start`, before 2038.

source.description: Where to block the dates: Fleetwire (`direct`) and any connected platforms.

put.description:
**Scope:** `bookings:write`

Changes the dates of an existing block. `:b_id` must be an unavailable period on this listing; real bookings return 404.

trip_start.description: A date and time, e.g. `2026-11-06 10:00:00` or ISO 8601.

delete.description:
**Scope:** `bookings:write`

Removes a block, including from any marketplace it was pushed to. Real bookings return 404.

get.description:
Your customers, newest first, paginated (follow `links.next`).

**Filters**

- `email` — exact match
- `phone` — any format; `(310) 555-0142`, `3105550142` and `+13105550142` all match
- `search` — part of a first name, last name or email (2+ characters)
- `updated_since` — ISO 8601; customers changed at or after this moment. Pair with the `customer.updated` webhook to keep a CRM in sync.
- `limit` — page size, 1–500 (default 100)

`bookings_count`, `total_spent_in_cents` and `last_trip_end` count real trips only — not canceled bookings or abandoned checkouts.

**Scope:** `customers:write`

- `first_name`, `last_name` (required)
- `email` and/or `phone` — at least one. Must not match another of your customers (`422` names the field).
- `dob` (YYYY-MM-DD), `address_1`, `address_2`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`, `country` (optional)

Returns `201` with the customer. Fires `customer.created`.

post.description:
Prices a trip with the same math checkout uses and says whether the vehicle is free. Nothing is saved, so call it as often as you like (120 per minute).

**Body**

- `l_id` (string, required)
- `start`, `end` (string, required) — local times in the listing's timezone
- `extras` (array, optional) — `[{"id": "<extra uuid>", "option": "<option uuid>"}]`. Omit `option` for the first one. Use `with=listings` on `GET /extras` to see what each listing offers. Required extras are always charged; listing one here picks its option.
- `coupon` (string, optional)
- `email` (string, optional) — needed only for coupons limited per customer

**Response**

- `available` — `false` if the vehicle is booked or blocked for those dates (buffer time included)
- `totals` — all in cents: `subtotal`, `discounts`, `taxes`, `total`, `security_deposit`, and `due_at_checkout` (what the renter pays now, per your payment settings)
- `checkout_url` — your storefront's checkout for this listing with the dates filled in. Send the renter there to book and pay; you'll get `reservation.created` when they do.

Delivery isn't priced here yet. Trips that break your booking rules (hours, lead time, trip length) return `422` with the reason under `errors.dates`.

start.description: A date and time, e.g. `2026-11-06 10:00:00` or ISO 8601.

get.description:
Returns bookings (not blocks), newest first, paginated.

**Filters**

- `trip_start` / `trip_end` — trips starting on/after, ending on/before
- `updated_since` — ISO 8601; only bookings changed at or after this moment. Use it to poll incrementally.
- `providers` — comma-separated sources, e.g. `direct,turo`
- `includeAbandoned=true` / `onlyAbandoned=true` — include unfinished checkouts
- `limit` — page size, 1–500 (default 100); follow `links.next` to page
- `include` — comma-separated: `renter`, `listing`, `listingImages`, `vehicle`, `payment`, `rentalAgreement`, `stripeIdentity`

**Trip and payment fields**

- `pickup_location` / `return_location` — where the trip starts and ends: the Turo trip's address, else the delivery address on the order, else the vehicle's branch pickup and return spots
- `odometer_start` / `odometer_end` — readings at pickup and return, typed by the host or captured from a connected car; in the company's distance unit
- `total` — the booked total, in cents
- `amount_paid_in_cents` — what the renter has paid on the order, refundable security deposits excluded; `null` when the booking has no order (Turo trips are paid out by Turo)
- `balance_due_in_cents` — still owed on the order

Amounts are visible only to tokens whose user can view order financials.

**Lookups** (return a single match instead of a list)

- `b_id` — one booking by ID
- `email` or `phone` — a customer's bookings

put.description:
**Scope:** `bookings:write`

Moves a booking to a new status and runs the same side effects as the dashboard (notifications, calendar sync).

`status` is one of: `pending_approval`, `reserved`, `started`, `stopped`, `complete`, `completed`, `canceled`, `archived`, `concept`.

post.description:
**Scope:** `charges:write`

For a toll or violation service the host connected with an API token: add one toll, violation or fee to a booking. It's billed on the booking's invoices and the host collects it from the renter. If the booking's invoice is already paid, it goes on a new invoice for that booking rather than reopening the paid one. (Services working with many hosts should use the Fleetwire Partner API instead: one key, no per-host tokens.)

- `provider` (string, required) — your service's short id, e.g. `myeztoll` (lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`)
- `external_id` (string, required) — your id for the charge. **Idempotent:** sending the same `external_id` with the same amount and kind returns the original with `200` and never bills twice. Different details under the same id return `409`.
- `kind` (required) — `toll`, `violation` or `fee`
- `amount_cents` (integer, required) — the road cost or fine
- `provider_fee_cents` (integer) — your fee, billed as its own line next to the charge
- `occurred_at` (ISO 8601, required except for `fee`) — when the toll was passed or the violation issued
- `description` (string) — shown to the renter on the invoice line, e.g. `E-ZPass NY — 3 tolls, Oct 10`
- `listing_id`, `plate`, `plate_state` — cross-checked against the booking's vehicle
- `authority`, `location`, `citation_number`, `violation_type` (`parking`, `red_light`, `speed`, `other`), `due_at`
- `document` (PDF file, multipart), `document_pdf` (base64) or `document_url` (public https link) — an itemized receipt, up to 5 MB
- `currency` (default `USD`)

**Refused (422)** when the charge isn't for that booking: a different `listing_id` or `plate`, or an `occurred_at` outside the trip. **404** for a booking that isn't yours. **409** when the booking has no order to bill, or the `external_id` conflicts.

`status` is `unbilled`, `billed` (on an unpaid invoice), `paid` or `voided`.

external_id.description: Your id for the charge. The idempotency key.

provider_fee_cents.description: Your fee, billed as its own line.

description.description: Shown on the renter's invoice line.

document_pdf.description: Itemized receipt PDF, base64. Up to 5 MB.

document_url.description: A public https link to the receipt PDF.

get.description: The charges sent to this booking, with whether each is paid yet. Use it to reconcile.

delete.description:
**Scope:** `charges:write`

For a toll the agency reversed or the host waived. If the renter hasn't paid it, it comes off the invoice. If they have, a refund line goes on a new invoice (the paid one never changes). Voiding twice is harmless.

get.description: Every event an endpoint can subscribe to.
Your company's webhook endpoints, including any Zapier created (`type: zapier`).

post.description:
**Scope:** `webhooks:write`

Registers a URL to receive events. The response includes `signing_secret` — **this is the only time it is shown**, so store it to verify deliveries.

- `url` (string, required) — public `https://` URL
- `events` (array, required) — event names from `GET /webhooks/events`
- `description` (string, optional)

get.description: One endpoint by its `id`.

put.description:
**Scope:** `webhooks:write`

Change any of `url`, `description`, `events` (replaces the list) or `status` (`enabled` / `disabled`). Disabled endpoints receive nothing.

schema.description: Send only the fields to change.

delete.description:
**Scope:** `webhooks:write`

Stops all deliveries to the endpoint. Returns `204 No Content`.

get.description: Every delivery attempt to the endpoint, newest first, 50 per page. `event_id` matches the `fleetwire-event-id` header; retries of one event share it.
Returns the company's add-ons (child seats, coolers, prepaid fuel…). Pass `with=listings` to include which listings each extra applies to.
Returns the company's coupon codes and the listings each applies to.
The companies that have you turned on.

The company's vehicles and their plates, one row per car. A listing with several identical units returns one row per unit, each with its own plate and `unit_id`, so `listing_id` can repeat. Paginated.

Rentals, with no renter details. Two ways to ask:

- **One lookup:** `plate` and `at` return the rental that had that plate at that moment, or an empty list. Optional: if you skip it, Fleetwire matches charges by plate and time itself.
- **A period:** `from` and `to` (at most 93 days apart) return every rental whose trip overlaps the window, paginated, cancelled ones included. Use it for per-rental fees such as a registration fee.

Send one pair or the other, not both. Unconfirmed booking requests are never listed.

post.description:
Send one toll, violation or fee. It's billed on the rental's order by the rental company's own rules.

With `rental_id`, the charge is checked against that rental: the plate must match the rental's vehicle and
`occurred_at` must fall within the trip (with a day either side). If not, you get `422` and nothing is billed.
Without `rental_id`, Fleetwire matches by `plate` and `occurred_at`; if no rental had the car then, the charge
is kept as `unmatched` for the rental company to review.

The receipt can be a multipart file (`document`), base64 (`document_pdf`) or a public `https` link
(`document_url`, downloaded once, no redirects). It must be a PDF of 5 MB or less.

**Idempotent:** the same `external_id` with the same amount and kind returns the original with `200`.
A different amount or kind under the same `external_id` returns `409`; use PATCH to change a charge.

toll.summary: A toll matched by plate and time

violation.summary: A violation for a known rental

fee.summary: A fee of yours (no occurred_at needed)

document.description: Itemized receipt PDF, up to 5 MB.

200.description: The charge. `200` means this was a retry of a charge Fleetwire already has, and the original is returned; `201` means it was newly created.

409.description: The `external_id` was already used for a charge with a different amount or kind.

error.message: This external_id was already used for a charge with different details. Use PATCH to change a charge.

get.description: The charge with its current status. Use it to reconcile.

patch.description:
| `status` | Also send | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `voided` | `reason`? | Taken off the renter's bill. If they already paid, they're refunded on a new invoice. |
| `amount_changed` | `amount_cents`, `reason`? | Re-billed at the new amount (`0` voids it). A paid amount is refunded and re-billed, never edited in place. |
| `paid_at_authority` | | Recorded; shown as `authority_status`. |
| `disputed` | | Recorded; shown as `authority_status`. |
| `dispute_resolved` | `amount_cents` | `0` voids the charge; another amount re-bills it. |

apiToken.description: An API token from **Settings → API tokens** in Fleetwire, sent as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Each token carries scopes: `read` for every GET, plus write scopes such as `bookings:write`.

partnerKey.description:
Your partner key, starting with `fwp_`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer fwp_…`. Keep it server-side.
Fleetwire can rotate it at any time; the old key stops working as soon as a new one is issued.

Forbidden.description: The token doesn't carry the scope this needs, or the plan doesn't include API access.

NotFound.description: Not found, or it isn't your company's.

errors.description: Each invalid field with its problems.

example.message: The email field must be a valid email address.

email: The email field must be a valid email address.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Wait for the `Retry-After` header (seconds).

PartnerInvalidKey.description: Missing, wrong or revoked partner key.

PartnerCompanyNotConnected.description: Unknown company, or it hasn't turned you on, or turned you off. Stop sending for this company.

error.message: This company has not turned on your integration, or has turned it off. Stop sending for this company.

PartnerNotFound.description: No charge with that `external_id` (or the company isn't connected; see `error.code`).

PartnerValidationFailed.description: The request is invalid. `error.fields` lists each problem.

occurred_at: This happened outside that rental_id's trip.

PartnerRateLimited.description: More than 600 requests in a minute. Wait for the `Retry-After` header (seconds).

activated_at.description: When the company turned you on.

unit_id.description: The rental company's own name for this car (for example `CAMRY-2`), when they have given it one. On a listing with several identical cars it tells the rows apart.

plate_state.description: State or province on the plate, when the rental company has entered it.

status.description: `canceled` rentals are listed by period so you can reverse a per-rental fee.

toll_plan.description: How the renter pays for tolls on this rental. `unlimited`: don't add individual tolls. `activation_plus_toll`: send each actual toll. `pay_per_use`: send each toll, with your fee in `provider_fee_cents` if you charge one. `null`: the rental company hasn't set a plan, so hold the toll for review. The rental company sets a default and can change it per rental. Treat a value you don't recognize like `null`.

source.description: Where the rental was booked: `direct` (through Fleetwire), `turo`, `getaround`, `outdoorsy`, `hirecar`, `shair` or `hq_rentals`. Marketplace trips such as Turo are billed through the marketplace, so use it to leave per-rental fees off them. New values may be added later; `null` means unknown.

external_id.description: Your id for this charge. The idempotency key.

kind.description: `fee` is a charge of yours that isn't a toll or violation, e.g. a registration fee.

provider_fee_cents.description: Your fee for this charge. Billed to the renter as its own line.

occurred_at.description: When it happened. Required unless `kind` is `fee`.

rental_id.description: The rental, if you know it. Otherwise matched by `plate` and `occurred_at`.

plate.description: Needed for matching when there's no `rental_id`.

due_at.description: When the authority wants it paid.

document_pdf.description: Itemized receipt PDF, base64-encoded. Up to 5 MB.

document_url.description: A public https link to the receipt PDF. Downloaded once, no redirects.

amount_cents.description: Required for `amount_changed` and `dispute_resolved`. `0` voids the charge.

match.description:
`provided`: you sent `rental_id`. `matched`: Fleetwire found the rental by plate and time.
`unmatched`: no rental had the car then; the rental company reviews it.

status.description:
`unmatched`: no rental found. `unbilled`: matched, but the rental has nothing to bill on yet.
`billed`: on the renter's invoice, not paid yet. `paid`: the renter paid that invoice.
`voided`: voided by you or the rental company.

fields.description: Present only on `validation_failed`. Each invalid field with its problems.
